title: bug: scripts/doctor.ps1 can never pass, because Run-Native names its argument array $Args and PowerShell's automatic $args replaces it with the empty unbound-argument list: `java -version` runs as bare `java` (usage text, exit 1) and -Full runs Gradle's default task instead of buildPlugin
description:
Filed by the 11-03 #6 defect hunt (task-cea8fa39, architect-1dd28c7c). Found by a hunt subagent; I re-ran both repros myself.

PROBLEM
scripts/doctor.ps1:14 declares `function Run-Native([string]$Cmd, [string[]]$Args)` and runs `& $Cmd @Args` at :23. In a simple (non-advanced) function, `$args` is PowerShell's automatic variable for the unbound arguments. It replaces the declared parameter, so inside the function $Args is always empty. As a result:
- :45 `Run-Native "java" @("-version")` runs bare `java`. That prints usage and exits 1, Run-Native throws "java exited with code 1", and under `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"` (:5) the script dies at "Checking Java...". On a machine without Java, Require-Command throws one line earlier. So doctor.ps1 fails on every machine.
- :51 `Run-Native $gradleBin @("--version")` would run Gradle with no task. It is never reached.
- :68 `Run-Native $gradleBin @("buildPlugin")` (the -Full build) would run Gradle's default task instead of buildPlugin. :70 would then report whatever stale zip build\distributions already holds.

EVIDENCE (Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.9711 on this host, HEAD 19d5e67a)
1. Minimal: `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File D:\moe-scratch\hunt-cea8\mine\args-shadow.ps1` prints
   `Cmd=[java] Args.Count=0 Args=[]`
   `Cmd=[java] Arguments.Count=1 Arguments=[-version]` (the same function with the parameter renamed)
   Output: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-cea8/mine/args-shadow.out.txt.
2. Run-Native copied verbatim (lines 14-33) with a recorder .cmd: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-cea8/B/doctor-ps1/run-native-harness.ps1, output run-native-harness.out.txt:
   - `Run-Native $fake @("buildPlugin")` gives `fake-tool argv=[]`, while a direct `& $fake buildPlugin` gives `fake-tool argv=[buildPlugin]`.
   - `Run-Native "java" @("-version")` prints `java.exe : Usage: java [options] <mainclass> [args...]` and then `THROWN: java exited with code 1`.
3. End to end, using a byte-identical copy (checked with cmp) at /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-cea8/B/doctor-ps1/scripts/doctor.ps1. The host has JDK 17.0.20, Node v24.16.0 and npm 11.15.0. Output, in doctor-ps1.out.txt: "== Moe Doctor ==", "Checking Node + npm...", "v24.16.0", "11.15.0", "Checking Java...", "java.exe : Usage: java [options] ...", "java exited with code 1", exit=1.

FIX DIRECTION
Rename the parameter (for example `[string[]]$Arguments`) and splat `@Arguments`. Don't turn the function advanced just to dodge the automatic variable. Make no other change to doctor.ps1's checks: doctor.sh's Java-is-optional asymmetry is out of scope.

FILES
- scripts/doctor.ps1
- scripts/tests/doctor-ps1.test.mjs (new test)
The test is Windows-only, using the repo convention `{ skip: process.platform !== 'win32' && 'Windows only' }`. It extracts the Run-Native FunctionDefinitionAst from scripts/doctor.ps1 with `[System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile` and runs it in a child `powershell.exe -NoProfile` against a recorder .cmd in a temp dir. That keeps java and Gradle out of the test.
Out of scope: scripts/moe-agent.* (the CQ-M07 lane). Note that moe-agent.ps1's `[object]$Args` parameters are on advanced functions, which bind correctly.

NOTE FOR QA
Run the test with Windows node (`node.exe --test scripts/tests/doctor-ps1.test.mjs` from a snapshot on a D:\ path). Under WSL node it skips.
definitionOfDone: `grep -niE '\$args\b' scripts/doctor.ps1` prints nothing (the parameter is renamed and every use follows it).

`node.exe --test scripts/tests/doctor-ps1.test.mjs` passes on Windows. The test extracts Run-Native from scripts/doctor.ps1 with the PowerShell parser and calls it with a recorder .cmd: `@("buildPlugin")` and `@("--version")` each reach the recorder as exactly that argv, and a recorder that exits 3 makes Run-Native throw a message containing "exited with code 3".
`[System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile` on scripts/doctor.ps1 reports 0 errors, and the diff touches only scripts/doctor.ps1 and the new test file.
